title: Updates and Amendments to the Civil Service Rules
summary: The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) is confirming the effective date of the direct final rule updating and amending obsolete and outdated provisions of the Civil Service Rules. OPM received no significant adverse comments and therefore confirms that the direct final rule became effective as scheduled.

title: Procedures for Settling Claims
summary: The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) confirms that the direct final rule updating the procedures for submitting certain administrative claims to OPM became effective as scheduled.

title: FLSA Claims and Compliance
summary: The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) confirms that the direct final rule updating provisions concerning Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) claims submissions to OPM became effective as scheduled.

title: Federal Employees' Retirement System; Present Value Conversion Factors for Spouses of Deceased Separated Employees
summary: The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) is confirming the effective date of its direct final rule revising the table of reduction factors for early commencing dates of survivor annuities paid to spouses of separated employees who die before the date on which they would be eligible for unreduced deferred annuities. OPM received no significant adverse comments during the comment period and confirms the rule was effective August 24, 2026.

title: Taking and Importing Marine Mammals; Taking Marine Mammals Incidental to Military Readiness Activities in the Northwest Training and Testing Study Area
summary: NMFS has received a request from the U.S. Department of the Navy (including the U.S. Navy and the U.S. Marine Corps (Navy)) and on behalf of the U.S. Coast Guard (Coast Guard); hereafter, Navy and Coast Guard are collectively referred to as Action Proponents) for authorization to take marine mammals incidental to training, testing, and modernization and sustainment of ranges conducted in the Northwest Training and Testing (NWTT) Study Area over the course of 7 years from November 2027 through November 2034. Pursuant to regulations implementing the Marine Mammal Protection Act (MMPA), NMFS is announcing receipt of the Action Proponents' request for the development and implementation of regulations governing the incidental taking of marine mammals and issuance of two 7-year Letters of Authorization (LOAs). NMFS invites the public to provide information, suggestions, and comments on the Action Proponents' application and request.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities: Submission for OMB Review, Comment Request; Environmental and Historic Preservation Screening Form
summary: The Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) will submit the information collection abstracted below to the Office of Management and Budget for review and clearance in accordance with the requirements of the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995. FEMA invites the general public to take this opportunity to comment on an extension of a currently approved information collection. In accordance with the requirements of the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995, this notice seeks comments concerning the information collection activities required to administer the Environmental and Historic Preservation Environmental Screening Form.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities: Proposed Collection; Comment Request; State, Tribe, and Territory Disaster Case Management (DCM) Federal Award
summary: The Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), as part of its continuing effort to reduce paperwork and respondent burden, invites the public to take this opportunity to comment on a revision of a currently approved information collection. In accordance with the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995, this notice seeks comments concerning information collected during the request by a State, Tribal, or territorial government for a Disaster Case Management (DCM) Federal award following a major disaster declaration.

title: Center for Scientific Review; Notice of Closed Meeting
Extension of Import Restrictions Imposed on Archaeological and Ethnological Material of Greece
summary: This document amends U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) regulations to reflect the extension of import restrictions on certain categories of archaeological and ecclesiastical ethnological material from the Hellenic Republic (Greece), which were originally published in CBP Decision (Dec.) 11-25 on December 1, 2011, and subsequently extended in 2016, and amended and extended in 2021 in CBP Dec. 21-16. The CBP regulations are being amended to reflect this further extension through November 21, 2031.

title: Caribbean Fishery Management Council 191st Public Hybrid Meeting
summary: The Caribbean Fishery Management Council (CFMC) will hold the 191st public hybrid meeting to address the items contained in the tentative agenda included in the SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION.

title: Accreditation and Approval of Intertek USA, Inc. (Texas City, TX), as a Commercial Gauger and Laboratory
summary: Notice is hereby given, pursuant to CBP regulations, that Intertek USA, Inc. (Texas City, TX), has been approved to gauge petroleum and certain petroleum products and accredited to test petroleum and certain petroleum products for customs purposes for the next three years as of October 28, 2025.

title: Privacy Act of 1974; Systems of Records
summary: Pursuant to the Privacy Act of 1974 and Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Circular No. A-108, notice is hereby given that the Drug Enforcement Administration (hereinafter DEA), a component within the United States Department of Justice (DOJ or Department), proposes to modify its system of records notice (SORN) JUSTICE/DEA-015, titled "Training Files" to be renamed JUSTICE/DEA-015 Training and Outreach Records in order to more precisely define all record categories, cover all applicable routine uses, and update the associated record practices.

title: Information Collection Activities; Submission to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for Review and Approval; Comment Request; Streamlined Supply Chain Information Collection Request
Information Collection; Federal Management Regulation; Statement of Witness; Standard Form 94
summary: Under the provisions of the Paperwork Reduction Act, the Regulatory Secretariat Division invites members of the public to comment on an extension to an existing information collection requirement regarding the common form SF-94, Statement of Witness.

title: National Institute of Standards and Technology Information Collection Activities; Submission to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for Review and Approval; Comment Request; Manufacturing Extension Partnership (MEP) Client Impact Survey
Agency Information Collection Activities; Submission to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for Review and Approval; Comment Request; Annual Integrated Economic Survey
Agency Information Collection Activities; Renewal of an Approved Information Collection: Generic Clearance of Customer Satisfaction Surveys
summary: In accordance with the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995, FMCSA announces its plan to submit the Information Collection Request (ICR) described below to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for review and approval and invites public comment. Executive Order (E.O.) 12862 directs Federal agencies to provide service to the public that matches or exceeds the best service available in the private sector. These principles were reaffirmed in E.O. 13571. In order to work continuously to ensure that the Agency's programs are effective and meet our customers' needs, FMCSA requests approval to renew an ICR titled, "Generic Clearance of Customer Satisfaction Surveys." This ICR allows FMCSA to continue collecting feedback on FMCSA's service delivery. By feedback the Agency means information that provides useful insights on perceptions and opinions but are not statistical surveys that yield quantitative results that can be generalized to the population of study.

title: Hours of Service (HOS) of Drivers; American Pyrotechnics Association (APA); Request To Include an Additional Member Company to Current APA HOS Exemptions
summary: FMCSA announces its decision to grant the American Pyrotechnics Association's (APA) application to add new member company North Star Fireworks LLC (North Star) to the APA's existing exemptions during the designated Independence Day periods. The exemptions allow drivers to exclude off-duty and sleeper berth time of any length from the calculation of the 14-hour limit and to use paper records of duty status (RODS) in lieu of electronic logging devices (ELDs). FMCSA has determined that the exemptions, subject to the terms and conditions set forth below, are likely to achieve a level of safety that is equivalent to, or greater than, the level of safety that would be achieved in the absence of the exemptions.

title: Granting of Requests for Early Termination of the Waiting Period Under the Premerger Notification Rules
Implementation of HAVANA Act of 2021
summary: This rule provides implementation by the Department of Homeland Security ("the Department" or "DHS") of the HAVANA Act of 2021. The HAVANA Act provides authority for agency heads to provide payments to certain individuals who have incurred qualifying injuries to the brain. This rule covers current and former Department of Homeland Security employees and their dependents.

title: Revised Non-foreign Overseas Per Diem Rates
summary: PRMA publishes this Civilian Personnel Per Diem Bulletin Number 333. Bulletin Number 333 lists current per diem rates prescribed for reimbursement of subsistence expenses while on official Government travel to Alaska, Hawaii, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, and the possessions of the U.S. The Calendar Year (CY) 2026 lodging and meal rate review for U.S. Virgin Islands resulted in rate changes for multiple locations.

title: Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and Plants; Threatened Species Status With Section 4(d) Rule for White Sands Pupfish and Critical Habitat Determination
summary: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service), propose to list the White Sands pupfish (Cyprinodon tularosa), a fish species from southcentral New Mexico, as a threatened species with protective regulations under section 4(d) of the Endangered Species Act of 1973, as amended (Act). This determination also serves as our 12-month finding on a petition to list the White Sands pupfish. After a review of the best scientific and commercial data available, we find that listing the species is warranted. If we finalize this rule as proposed, it would add this species to the List of Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and extend the Act's protections to the species. All areas meeting the definition of critical habitat for the White Sands pupfish occur on Department of War (DoW) owned facilities and are exempt from designation as critical habitat in accordance with section 4(a)(3)(B) of the Act. Therefore, we are not proposing any areas as critical habitat for the White Sands pupfish.

title: Pacific Island Fisheries; Marine Conservation Plan for Pacific Insular Areas Other Than American Samoa, Guam, and the Northern Mariana Islands; Western Pacific Sustainable Fisheries Fund
summary: NMFS announces approval of a Marine Conservation Plan (MCP) for Pacific Insular Areas other than American Samoa, Guam, and the Northern Mariana Islands.

title: Magnuson-Stevens Act Provisions; Fisheries Off West Coast States; Pacific Coast Groundfish Fishery; 2026 Tribal Fishery Allocations for Pacific Whiting; Reapportionment Between Tribal and Non-Tribal Sectors
summary: This document announces the reapportionment of 29,130 metric tons of Pacific whiting from the Tribal allocation to the non-Tribal commercial fishery sectors via automatic actions on September 14, and 23, and October 5, 2026. This reapportionment is to allow full utilization of the Pacific whiting resource.

title: Pacific Island Fisheries; Marine Conservation Plan for the Pacific Insular Area for the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands; Western Pacific Sustainable Fisheries Fund
summary: NMFS announces approval of a Marine Conservation Plan (MCP) for the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands (CNMI).

title: 60-Day Notice of Intent To Seek Extension of Approval: Appeals of Decisions Issued Under Delegated Authorities and Labor Arbitration Decisions
summary: As required by the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (PRA), the Surface Transportation Board (STB or Board) gives notice of its intent to seek approval from the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for approval of an existing collection in use without an OMB control number regarding appeals of decisions issued under delegated authorities and labor arbitration decisions, as described below.

title: Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and Plants; Endangered Species Status for Mazama Newt
summary: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service), propose to list the Mazama newt (Taricha granulosa mazamae), an amphibian species from the Crater Lake caldera in Crater Lake National Park in Klamath County, Oregon, as an endangered species under the Endangered Species Act of 1973, as amended (Act). This determination also serves as our 12-month finding on a petition to list the Mazama newt. After a review of the best scientific and commercial data available, we find that listing the species is warranted. If we finalize this rule as proposed, it would add this species to the List of Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and extend the Act's protections to the species. We find that designating critical habitat for this species is not determinable at this time.

title: Petition for Rulemaking of Alden Graham
summary: Please take notice that the Federal Trade Commission ("Commission") received a petition for rulemaking from Alden Graham and has published that petition online at https://www.regulations.gov. The Commission invites written comments concerning the petition. Publication of this petition is pursuant to the Commission's Rules of Practice and Procedure and does not affect the legal status of the petition or its final disposition.

title: Designated Reserve Ratio for 2027
summary: Pursuant to the Federal Deposit Insurance Act (FDI Act), the Board of Directors (Board) of the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) designates that the Designated Reserve Ratio (DRR) for the Deposit Insurance Fund shall remain at 2 percent for 2027. The Board is publishing this notice as required by the FDI Act.

title: Draft Policy Update to the NIH Policy for Data and Safety Monitoring; Correction
summary: The National Institutes of Health (NIH), Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), published a document in the Federal Register of November 17, 2026. That notice requires a correction in the ADDRESSES section.

title: Proposed Collection; Comment Request
summary: In accordance with the requirements of the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (PRA), the Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA) is seeking public comments concerning an information collection known as "Members of the Banks," which has been assigned control number 2590-0003 by the Office of Management and Budget (OMB). FHFA intends to submit the information collection to OMB for review and approval of a three-year extension of the control number, which is due to expire on November 30, 2026.

title: Proposed Collection; Comment Request
summary: In accordance with the requirements of the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (PRA), the Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA) is seeking public comments concerning an information collection known as "Federal Home Loan Bank Capital Stock," which has been assigned control number 2590-0002 by the Office of Management and Budget (OMB). FHFA intends to submit the information collection to OMB for review and approval of a three-year extension of the control number, which is due to expire on November 30, 2026.

title: Special Local Regulations; Annual Marine Events on the Colorado River, Between Davis Dam (Bullhead City, Arizona) and Headgate Dam (Parker, Arizona), BlueWater Resort and Casino Thanksgiving Regatta, Colorado River, Parker, AZ
summary: The Coast Guard will enforce special local regulations for the BlueWater Resort and Casino Thanksgiving Regatta from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m. on November 26, 2026, through 28, 2026, to provide for the safety of life on navigable waterways during this event. Our regulation for marine events within the Southwest Coast Guard District identifies the regulated area for this event in Parker, AZ. During the enforcement periods, the operator of any vessel in the regulated area must comply with directions from the Patrol Commander or any Official Patrol displaying a Coast Guard ensign.

title: Environmental Impact Statements; Notice of Availability
Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes
summary: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain The Boeing Company Model 737-600, -700, -700C, -800, and -900 series airplanes. This AD was prompted by a review of the autothrottle (A/T) cruise thrust split monitor (MONFD) and the determination that there is a potential for latent loss of spoiler sensor position data or erroneous spoiler sensor position data. This AD requires repetitive aileron built-in test equipment (BITE) tests of the digital flight control system and applicable on-condition actions. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Waivers and Alternative Requirements for Community Development Block Grant Disaster Recovery (CDBG-DR) and Community Development Block Grant Mitigation (CDBG-MIT) Grantees
summary: This notice governs Community Development Block Grant disaster recovery (CDBG-DR) and Community Development Block Grant mitigation (CDBG-MIT) funds awarded under the appropriations acts identified below. In response to grantee requests, this notice provides a general waiver and alternative requirement for all grantees that received CDBG- DR and CDBG-MIT funds for disasters occurring in 2015 to 2019, permitting buyout activities consistent with Universal Notice requirements. This notice also provides specific waivers and alternative requirements for the State of South Carolina and for Hawaii County, HI, for grants provided under the public laws cited herein.

title: Submission for OMB Review; Comment Request
New Postal Products
summary: The Commission is noticing a recent Postal Service filing for the Commission's consideration concerning a negotiated service agreement. This notice informs the public of the filing, invites public comment, and takes other administrative steps.

title: Submission for OMB Review; Comment Request
Product-Specific Guidances; Draft and Revised Draft Guidances for Industry; Availability
summary: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or Agency) is announcing the availability of additional draft and revised draft product-specific guidances. The draft guidances provide product-specific recommendations on, among other things, the design of bioequivalence (BE) studies to support abbreviated new drug applications (ANDAs). In the Federal Register of June 11, 2010, FDA announced the availability of a guidance for industry titled "Bioequivalence Recommendations for Specific Products" that explained the process that would be used to make product-specific guidances available to the public on FDA's website. The draft guidances identified in this notice were developed using the process described in that guidance.

title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus SAS Airplanes
summary: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Airbus SAS Model A330-841 and A330-941 airplanes. This AD was prompted by a report of cracks on the discharge outlet of certain engine fire extinguisher bottles. This AD requires modification of affected fire extinguisher bottles and prohibits the installation of affected parts. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Air Plan Approval; Oklahoma; Update to Materials Incorporated by Reference
summary: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is updating the materials that are incorporated by reference (IBR) into the Oklahoma State Implementation Plan (SIP). The regulations affected by this update have been previously submitted by the State of Oklahoma and approved by the EPA. This update affects the materials that are available for public inspection at the EPA Regional Office and the National Archives and Records Administration.

title: Cotton Board Rules and Regulations: Adjusting Supplemental Assessment on Imports (2025 Amendments)
summary: The Agricultural Marketing Service (AMS) is amending the Cotton Board Rules and Regulations to decrease the value assigned to imported cotton for the purposes of calculating supplemental assessments collected for use by the Cotton Research and Promotion Program. This amendment is required each year to ensure that assessments collected on imported cotton, and the cotton content of imported products, will be the same as those paid on domestically produced cotton. In addition, AMS is updating the Import Assessment Table to account for changes since the last assessment adjustment in 2024.

title: Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes
summary: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all The Boeing Company Model 757 airplanes. This AD was prompted by reports of crack damage at existing reinforcing repairs in the fuselage frame lower lobe areas in certain sections. This AD requires doing an inspection for any existing reinforcing repairs in the fuselage frame lower lobe areas in certain sections and applicable on-condition actions. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Board of Overseers of the Malcolm Baldrige National Quality Award
summary: The Board of Overseers of the Malcolm Baldrige National Quality Award (Board of Overseers or Board) will meet in open session on Thursday, December 10, 2026. The purpose of this meeting is to review and discuss the work of the Baldrige Performance Excellence Program and its private-sector partners to implement and improve the Malcolm Baldrige National Quality Award (Award), and to provide recommendations to the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) as the Board deems necessary. Details on the agenda are noted in the SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION section of this notice.

title: Air Plan Approval; Arkansas; Update to Materials Incorporated by Reference
summary: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is updating the materials that are incorporated by reference (IBR) into the Arkansas State Implementation Plan (SIP). The regulations affected by this update have been previously submitted by the State of Arkansas and approved by the EPA. This update affects the materials that are available for public inspection at the EPA Regional Office and the National Archives and Records Administration.

title: Air Plan Approval; Kentucky; Campbell-Clermont Area Maintenance Plan for the 2010 1-Hour SO2 NAAQS; Withdrawal of Direct Final Rule
summary: Due to the receipt of adverse comments, the U.S Environmental Protection Agency (EPA or Agency) is withdrawing the September 25, 2026, direct final rule that approved the second 10-year maintenance plan for the Kentucky portion of the Campbell-Clermont, Kentucky-Ohio maintenance area ("Campbell-Clermont, KY-OH Area" or "Area") for the 2010 1- hour sulfur dioxide (SO<INF>2</INF>) National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS).

title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters
summary: The FAA is superseding Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2025-13- 09, which applied to all Airbus Helicopters Model AS-365N2, AS 365 N3, EC 155B, EC155B1, SA-365N, and SA-365N1 helicopters. AD 2025-13-09 required inspecting the tightening torque, reporting the results of the inspections, and, depending on the results of the inspection, taking corrective action. Since the FAA issued AD 2025-13-09, the manufacturer determined that additional inspections of the main rotor (MR) servo-controls nut torque are required. This AD retains some of the actions of AD 2025-13-09 and requires additional inspections and, depending on the results of the inspection, corrective actions. This AD also requires reporting certain information to the manufacturer. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Sunshine Act Meeting
Draft 2026 Marine Mammal Stock Assessment Reports
summary: NMFS reviewed the Alaska, Atlantic, and Pacific regional marine mammal stock assessment reports (SARs) in accordance with the Marine Mammal Protection Act (MMPA). SARs for marine mammals in all three regions were revised to include new information. NMFS is soliciting public comments on the draft 2026 SARs. We will consider all comments that are received by the close of the comment period.
